title: Safety and pilot efficacy of a mobile app-based decision support system for exercise in type 1 diabetes
summary: We are aiming to test a recent produced prototype CGM-based exercise app (1:1 information from the EASD/ISPAD exercise position statement [1, 2]) for time in range (TIR; 70-180 mg/dL) around continuous moderate-intensity exercise, high-intensity interval exercise and resistance training against the recommendation approach (control phase) and a paper based EASD/ISPAD position statement group

interventions.name: Use of a prototype CGM-based exercise app for time in range around different types of exercise
Use of a paper based EASD/ISPAD position statement approach for time in range around different types of exercise

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Adults with T1D (as diagnosed clinically) ≥12 months 
2) Treated with multiple daily insulin injections ≥12 months 
3) Body mass index 18.0─29.9 kg/m2 (both inclusive) 
4) Mass-specific peak oxygen consumption (VO2peak) >20 ml/kg/min 
5) HbA1c ≤10% (86 mmol/mol)
6) Already using rtCGM or isCGM ≥ 3months
Exclusion criteria:
1) Recurrent severe hypoglycaemia (>severe hypoglycaemia during the past 12 months) 
2) Hypoglycaemia unawareness 
3) Hospitalisation for diabetic ketoacidosis during the previous 12 months
